verdict.rationale: NY DTF documents a sanctioned third-party rail: with a client's authorization, a tax professional can review the client's filing and payment history, view bills and notices, and respond on the client's behalf through Online Services. It also points businesses to approved tax-preparation software for filing. The documentation is a single summary sentence, so the scope and mechanics of the delegation are unproven; employee sub-users are first-party access, not a third-party rail, and earn no credit. Missing for 10: documentation of how authorization is granted or revoked (designee or power-of-attorney process), the scopes of delegated permissions, an authorized-provider or registered-agent registry, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company

citations.quote: With your client’s authorization, you can review their filing and payment history, view copies of their bills and notices, and respond on their behalf.
Use tax preparation approved software to submit Form CT-5.
